title: Eggs Benedict
subtitle: poached eggs, hollandaise, and ham on toasted muffin
excerpt: Eggs Benedict is the benchmark brunch dish. Poached eggs sit on toasted English muffins with ham and hollandaise sauce. The hollandaise is made here as part of the recipe -- take care with the heat and it will come together smoothly.
sourceNotes: Said to have been created at Delmonico's restaurant in New York in the late 19th century. The dish became a brunch staple across the English-speaking world during the 20th century.

content.text: The hollandaise is the tricky part. Keep the heat low and add the butter slowly -- too fast or too hot and the sauce will split. Have everything else ready before you start so you can serve immediately.

items.prepNote: use 4 slices of Canadian bacon or smoked ham
use 2 English muffins, split and toasted
use 4 egg yolks for the hollandaise

content.text: Make the hollandaise: put the egg yolks and a tablespoon of water in a heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water. Do not let the bowl touch the water.
Whisk constantly until the yolks are thick and pale and leave a trail when lifted, about 5 minutes.
Remove the bowl from the heat. Slowly whisk in the melted butter a little at a time. Add the lemon juice, mustard, and cayenne. Season and keep warm.
Warm the ham in a dry pan. Toast the muffins.
Bring a large pan of water to a gentle simmer. Add the vinegar. Crack each egg into a cup, then slide it into the water. Poach for 3 minutes for a soft yolk.
Place muffin halves on plates. Top each with ham, a poached egg, and a spoonful of hollandaise. Serve at once.

items.cause: Heat too high or butter added too fast
items.fix: Whisk a new egg yolk in a clean bowl and very slowly whisk in the split sauce.
Keep the water at a bare simmer. Fresher eggs hold their shape better.

items.symptom: Everything gets cold while you work
items.cause: Too many components to finish at once
items.fix: Keep muffins warm in the oven, keep hollandaise over hot water, and work fast with the eggs.

content.text: Eggs Benedict became a brunch institution across America, Britain, and Australia in the 20th century. It is the dish that made hollandaise sauce a household word. The combination of butter-rich sauce, runny yolk, and salty ham on toast hits every comfort note at once. It is a weekend treat that rewards the effort it takes.
